task: How do I add the server to Codex?

evals.prompt: How do I add our 'Harborline' MCP server to Codex using the CLI?
evals.expected_output: You should run the command `codex mcp add harborline --url https://appatools.com/mcp-studio/api/mcp/your-server-name` in the Codex CLI to add the server.
assertions: The command to add an MCP server in the CLI is 'codex mcp add <name> --url <url>'.
The example server URL format is 'https://appatools.com/mcp-studio/api/mcp/your-server-name'.
It's specified that you can use the command line to add the server, confirming it can be done without the desktop app.

evals.prompt: Can you guide me on adding a private server and what I need to change in the configuration?
evals.expected_output: To add a private server, you need to make it private in MCP Studio, create an access token, and set the 'bearer_token_env_var' in 'config.toml' to the variable name holding the token.
assertions: You must create an access token starting with 'mcps_live_' as part of connecting a private server.
The 'bearer_token_env_var' in 'config.toml' takes the variable's name, never the token itself.
The setup requires using 'http_headers = { "Authorization" = "Bearer <token>" }' if you choose to send the token directly.

evals.prompt: What steps do I follow to add the server using the ChatGPT desktop app?
evals.expected_output: You need to open Settings, select MCP servers, add your server with a name, choose Streamable HTTP, paste the URL, save, and then restart.
assertions: You first open Settings and then select MCP servers in the ChatGPT desktop app.
After selecting 'Add server', you enter a name and paste the server URL.
The server should be saved and you need to select 'Restart' to finalize the process.

evals.prompt: If I add a server but nothing appears when using '/mcp', what should I check?
evals.expected_output: You should check that the URL contains '/api/mcp/' and ensure you start a new session, as the server won't appear in an already open chat.
assertions: You must check that the URL of the server contains '/api/mcp/'.
If the server does not appear, starting a new session is necessary for Codex to recognize the newly added server.
The guide states that a startup message indicating a missing environment variable means the variable was not set or was incorrectly referenced.
